The map downloads tiles from %2$s\'s tile server, which sees your IP address and the area you\'re looking at; a place search runs on the phone over the offline map\'s road names and goes to OpenStreetMap\'s Nominatim service only when you choose to search online. Offline maps, work zones, the stalkerware list and the setting that names the tile server come signed from GitHub, and so, once a day, do the relay list, the keys those files are signed with and a note of the newest Clairix version. Messages and calls go through the Clairix relay, which cannot read them and is not told who sent them; live traffic is sent to it as anonymous road-segment speeds it can read but cannot tie to you. With Share traffic data on (Drive\'s route options) the box around a route you navigate or look at also goes through the relay to HERE and TomTom for incidents; they see the relay, not you. With push wake-ups set up, the relay sends your push server a POST saying only \"wake\" when something arrives; with Connect through Tor on, everything Clairix says to relays goes through the Tor network. Evidence leaves the phone only when you export it. Messages and calls are end-to-end encrypted; the relay sees neither what they say nor who sent them. Your keys, contacts and history are stored on this phone only. Everything Clairix says to relays goes through Tor, so no relay, this one or another, learns this phone\'s network address, and the network it is on does not learn which relay it uses. Nothing goes out directly while Tor is connecting. Slower, and uses more data. With Online off, Tor sleeps when nothing has needed it for five minutes and starts again with the next request, which then waits a few seconds. Calls do not go through Tor: during a call the relay\'s call server sees this phone\'s address. While Tor is on, a call goes only through the relay\'s TURN server, and is refused when the relay offers none, so the contact never learns it.

Bluetooth reaches a few tens of metres; phones with Bluetooth\'s long-range mode (shown above) reach several times farther between each other, out in the open. A message moves when phones pass each other. Photos, videos and calls stay for the relay. A contact can be reached only after one message has gone through the relay, which is how the two phones\' sessions start. Messages are carried for %1$s hours and at most %2$s hops. The relay keeps trying as well; whichever copy arrives second is dropped.
